assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors turn a Cas9 scaffold into a programmable nucleobase-modifying enzyme: deaminase chemistry applied to a single nucleotide in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks. It converts a biological process into a defined chemical reaction and gave biologists a general tool; the impact on genome engineering and therapy development is large and original.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental program; Komor (C-to-T) and Gaudelli (A-to-G, requiring an evolved TadA deaminase) made the decisive first-author contributions. Nishida/Kondo (Target-AID) were contemporaneous and could be argued; a Liu-only or Liu plus trainees configuration is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old, widely reproduced in many labs, with first clinical use in patients. Interpretation is stable. Timing is plausible but still early relative to typical lag.
uncertainties: Priority and credit relative to Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID work
Whether the committee wishes to recognise trainees alongside Liu
Long-term clinical safety (off-target deamination) is not yet fully known

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation is a new chemical modality: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to remove a target protein. The mechanism (ternary complex, ubiquitin transfer, cereblon as the thalidomide target) is chemically well defined and has changed drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and launched PROTACs; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target underpinning molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others contributed key advances, so a three-person limit forces hard choices and the PROTAC and glue strands may belong to different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are advanced, with late-stage trials, and the mechanism has been reproduced and extended across many laboratories. Maturity is good but regulatory validation is still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among PROTAC pioneers versus molecular-glue discoverers
Compound discovery whose strands may need separate recognition
Approval outcomes pending

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved the chemical problem of encapsulating and delivering nucleic acids into cells, enabling siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines. The pKa-tuned lipid design is a clear, original chemical solution with enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the lipid nanoparticle encapsulation and ionizable-lipid concepts, with Hope and Madden central in the early work; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan made important later contributions. Credit is distributed across academia and industry and is not cleanly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale by approved siRNA therapeutics and COVID-19 vaccines; independent confirmation is overwhelming. Recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize touched adjacent mRNA science.
uncertainties: Overlap with the mRNA-focused 2023 Medicine prize
Credit split between academic originators and later optimisers
Patent disputes may colour the attribution record

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis, built on reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule clustering, transformed genomics and made nucleic-acid analysis a chemical readout at unprecedented scale. Importance and lasting impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa chemistry; Mayer and colleagues contributed clustering and parallel amplification ideas; Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform is a competing strand. Allocation among these contributions is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous, independently reproduced everywhere. The risk is that the discovery is long established and the field leans toward Medicine.
uncertainties: Contested allocation among Solexa, 454 and Lynx strands
Whether the committee views it as chemistry or as a technology prize
Several decades since the original inventions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A modification established an epitranscriptomic layer with writers, erasers and readers, linking RNA chemistry to gene regulation. FTO as an m6A demethylase and transcriptome-wide mapping are conceptually original and chemically concrete.
assessment.attribution: He identified the demethylase and reader biology and proposed the reversible-modification concept; Jaffrey and Rechavi, with Dominissini, developed transcriptome-wide mapping. Several other labs contributed methods and mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: Broadly replicated, though some quantitative claims depend on mapping methods whose resolution and antibody specificity remain debated. Biological roles in disease are still being worked out.
uncertainties: Reproducibility and quantification issues in antibody-based m6A mapping
Disputed stoichiometry and functional claims for specific sites
Overlap with the 2023-style recognition of RNA base modification

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made routine solid-phase synthesis of defined DNA possible, supplying primers, probes, genes and therapeutic oligonucleotides. It is the enabling chemistry beneath much of molecular biology and a clean, foundational chemical invention.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite approach and the first practical synthesis; Hood's role is in automation and instrument commercialisation rather than the chemistry. A single-laureate award or a pairing is conceivable.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of universal use is as mature as it gets. Recognition is very late, which is a minor concern about relevance of timing but not about validity.
uncertainties: Credit for automation versus the underlying chemistry
Contributions of other nucleotide chemists in the 1980s are not in the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single nucleic-acid molecules through ionic current, engineering protein pores into analytical instruments and delivering long-read sequencing. Original and impactful, combining molecular engineering and single-molecule measurement.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz demonstrated single-strand translocation; Bayley engineered pores and chemistry for sensing; Akeson showed base-level discrimination with a polymerase motor. Five credited names exceed the limit and allocation is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: Commercial platforms now give independent validation, though accuracy and motor chemistry are still evolving. The interpretation of the current signal is stable.
uncertainties: Priority among the founding concept, pore engineering and enzyme-motor strands
Three-laureate limit leaves out Branton and Kasianowicz
Sequencing accuracy claims continue to evolve

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion uses orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs to incorporate noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, a general chemical tool for installing new functional groups in biology. Original and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and coworkers established the approach in E. coli and yeast, with Wang as the lead experimentalist in the early work; Chin extended it to higher organisms and quadruplet codons; Yokoyama contributed structural and pyrrolysine-related work.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely over two decades and routinely applied, though efficiency and yield limits remain. Recognition is plausible and maturity is good.
uncertainties: Possible competing credit for Yokoyama and Mehl
Practical yield limitations in some systems
Whether this prize would be seen as incremental on earlier directed-evolution recognition
